note: Audited false positives from scripts/scan_history.py. A history scan cannot be annotated in place: an inline `pragma: allowlist secret` fixes the working tree but the historical blob still contains the un-annotated line, and rewriting published history over a docstring placeholder would be absurd. So triage decisions live here, keyed by path and detector, and every entry must carry a reason. An entry without one fails the scan rather than suppressing anything.

entries.reason: A docstring documenting the API-key request body shape: `Body: {"api_key": "tpllm_..."}`. The matched value is the literal placeholder `tpllm_...`. The Secret Keyword plugin fires on the key name, not on the value. The working-tree line now carries an inline allowlist pragma; this entry covers the historical blobs, which cannot be annotated retroactively.

The same audited false positive as the entry above, at the path it occupied before the package was renamed from `lltpm` to `tpllm`. The historical blobs still live at `src/lltpm/dashboard.py` and always will: a rename moves the working tree, not the commits that came before it. Triage is keyed by path, so the rename needs both spellings or a reviewed finding reappears as a publication blocker for no reason. Same docstring, same literal placeholder `tpllm_...`, same conclusion.
